description: Add a rep-entered 'Add-on Services' capability to the Send Quotation dialog (src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx). Reps bundle extra services (e.g. 'CA Services', 'Signage Board Services') with a quote. Add a two-column (Service Name + Amount) repeatable input section in the dialog, with an 'Add more service' button and per-row removal, and render the entered non-empty add-ons as a new clearly-labeled table section INSIDE the quotation email HTML (so it appears in Preview and in the sent email). This is additive: it must NOT regress the existing multi-state selection, price overrides, per-row plan removal, single-state+city path, preview, or send. This is purely email-content; no DB/schema change. Work on a single new branch off latest origin/main.
steps: Create and check out a new branch off the LATEST origin/main: `git checkout -B feat/quotation-addon-services origin/main`. Confirm the file already contains selectedStates[], priceOverrides, removedRowKeys, displayPlans (PR #65 work) before editing so you build on top of it and do not regress it.

In the component SendQuotationDialog, add new state: `const [addonServices, setAddonServices] = useState<{ name: string; amount: string }[]>([]);` (amount kept as string for a controlled input; parsed to number only when building HTML).

Add handlers near the existing removeRow/toggleState handlers: addAddonRow (append `{ name: '', amount: '' }`), updateAddonName(index, value), updateAddonAmount(index, value), removeAddonRow(index) (filter by index). Keep them immutable (map/filter/spread), matching the existing setPriceOverrides style.

In the useEffect that runs when `open` becomes true (the block that does setSelectedStates/setSelectedCity/setServiceType/setPriceOverrides/setRemovedRowKeys/setStatePopoverOpen/setPreviewing), add `setAddonServices([]);` so a fresh dialog always starts empty and add-ons never leak between different leads.

Add an 'Add-on Services' UI section in the editor form, placed AFTER the existing 'Pricing Preview' block and BEFORE the 'Email summary' block, inside the same `<div className="px-6 py-4 space-y-5">` ScrollArea content. Use a `<Label className="text-xs font-semibold">` header (e.g. 'Add-on Services' with a muted hint like '(optional extra services)'). For each row in addonServices render a flex row with: a Service Name text input, an Amount number input, and an X remove button. Match existing styling conventions in this file: reuse the same raw input classNames used by the pricing editor's number input (`w-... text-sm border rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 focus:ring-1 focus:ring-primary/30 focus:outline-none`) OR the shadcn Input component if you import it - pick ONE consistent approach and stay type-clean. For the remove button reuse the exact X-button pattern already used for removeRow (lucide `X` icon, `h-3.5 w-3.5`, aria-label). Below the rows render a Button (variant 'outline', size small) labeled 'Add more service' that calls addAddonRow. When addonServices is empty, still show the 'Add more service'/'Add-on Service' button so the rep can start; clicking it reveals the first row (this satisfies the user's 'when clicked, two columns Service name & Amount appear' requirement).

Wire the inputs: Service Name input value={row.name} onChange updates via updateAddonName(i, e.target.value); Amount input type='number' min={0} value={row.amount} onChange updates via updateAddonAmount(i, e.target.value). Show a rupee hint next to the amount input (e.g. a leading rupee char or placeholder) consistent with formatINR usage; do not force-parse in the input handler (store the raw string).
Extend buildQuotationHtml's opts type to add an optional param: `addons?: { name: string; amount: number }[]`. Destructure it with a default: `const { ..., addons = [] } = opts;`.

Inside buildQuotationHtml, build an add-ons section string only when addons.length > 0. Build rows mirroring the pricing table's inline-style pattern: striped backgrounds (`idx % 2 === 0 ? '#fff' : '#F8FAFC'`), same padding/border/font styles, Service Name in the left cell (color #1E293B, font-weight 600), Amount right-aligned via formatINR(a.amount). GST TREATMENT: render add-ons as FLAT amounts (no GST column) for clarity and safety - the amount the rep types is the amount charged. Include a bold subtotal row summing all add-on amounts, right-aligned and formatted with formatINR. Wrap it in a section styled like the PRICING TABLE section: a `<tr><td style="background:#fff;padding:32px 28px" class="pad-lg">` block with a centered header (small uppercase eyebrow label in #1E4DB7 e.g. 'ADD-ON SERVICES' and a larger #0F172A title e.g. 'Additional Services You Selected'), then a table with a navy (#0A1F4D) header row containing 'SERVICE' (left) and 'AMOUNT' (right) th cells styled like the existing pricing th cells (color #FFE39A). Keep all styles inline and table-based (email-safe). Do NOT touch the existing static marketing ADD-ONS showcase section (Meeting Rooms/Day Passes/etc.).

Interpolate the new section string into the returned HTML template immediately AFTER the closing of the PRICING TABLE section (the `` that ends the block containing `${pricingRows}` and the two note boxes) and BEFORE the `` comment. If addons is empty the interpolated variable is an empty string so nothing renders.

In the emailHtml useMemo, compute the parsed, filtered add-on list: map addonServices, trim name, parse amount (Number), and KEEP ONLY rows where name is non-empty AND amount is a finite number > 0 (filter out blank/garbage rows). Pass the result as `addons` to buildQuotationHtml. Add `addonServices` to the useMemo dependency array.

Do a final self-review read of the whole component to confirm: (a) existing displayPlans/priceOverrides/removedRowKeys/multi-state/single-state+city/preview/send logic is untouched, (b) all new state/handlers are typed and used, (c) no unused imports were added, (d) JSX is balanced, (e) the emailHtml deps array includes addonServices.

Commit on the feature branch with a conventional message, e.g. `git add src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx && git commit -m "feat(quotation): add rep-entered add-on services (name + amount) rendered in quote email"`. Do NOT push. Do NOT commit anything under .agents/.
acceptance_criteria: SendQuotationDialog has addonServices state of type { name: string; amount: string }[] with add/edit-name/edit-amount/remove handlers, and it is reset to [] in the open-effect alongside the other resets.

The dialog form shows an 'Add-on Services' section with a two-column (Service Name + Amount) repeatable row layout, an 'Add more service' button to append rows, and a per-row X remove control, styled consistently with the rest of the dialog.

buildQuotationHtml accepts an optional addons param and, when non-empty, renders a new email-safe table section (navy header, striped rows, rupee-formatted amounts, bold subtotal) placed right after the main pricing table and before the multi-year section. When empty, nothing new renders.

emailHtml useMemo parses addonServices, filters out rows with blank name or non-positive/non-numeric amount, passes them as addons, and lists addonServices in its dependency array. Entered add-ons therefore appear in both Preview and the sent email.
Existing multi-state selection, price overrides, per-row plan removal, single-state+city filtering, preview, and send behavior are unchanged.

No em dashes introduced in any code comments or content. No unused imports. Work committed on branch feat/quotation-addon-services off latest origin/main; nothing committed to main; nothing under .agents/ committed.

Perform careful code inspection: confirm the addons param type matches the parsed shape { name: string; amount: number }[]; confirm the emailHtml deps array includes addonServices; confirm the on-open effect resets addonServices; confirm JSX balance and no unused imports.
Grep-verify the new section is interpolated exactly once between the pricing table and the MULTI-YEAR DISCOUNT comment.
Confirm `git log` on feat/quotation-addon-services shows the new commit and `git diff origin/main --stat` shows only src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx changed.
findings: Implemented on branch feat/quotation-addon-services off origin/main (706367f). Only src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx changed (+104/-3), committed as 3d5f8bc. Added addonServices state ({name,amount}[], amount kept as string), addAddonRow/updateAddonName/updateAddonAmount/removeAddonRow handlers (immutable map/filter/spread), and reset via setAddonServices([]) in the open-effect. Added an 'Add-on Services' UI section between Pricing Preview and Email summary: a text input for name, a number input for amount (with a leading rupee char), a per-row X remove button reusing the existing removeRow button pattern, and an outline size-sm 'Add more service' button; when empty only the button shows so the first click reveals the first row. Reused the raw input classNames from the pricing editor (no new imports; Button/Label/X already imported). Extended buildQuotationHtml opts with optional addons?: {name;amount:number}[] (destructured with default []), and built an email-safe add-ons section (navy #0A1F4D header with #FFE39A th cells, striped rows, formatINR amounts, bold subtotal row summing amounts, FLAT amounts with NO GST column per the decision) interpolated exactly once after the pricing table and before the MULTI-YEAR DISCOUNT comment. emailHtml useMemo parses/trims/filters add-ons (keep only name!=='' && Number.isFinite(amount) && amount>0) and passes them as addons; added addonServices to the deps array. Did NOT touch the static marketing ADD-ONS showcase section, and did not regress selectedStates/priceOverrides/removedRowKeys/displayPlans/single-state+city/preview/send. No em dashes in added lines (the one em dash at line 834 is pre-existing from PR #65).
